Recap of Lecture 06
❖Based on the way pixels get excited on a screen, a display device 
can be of two types:
▪ Vector Scan (also know as random scan or calligraphic devices) :  
a set of dedicated pixels along a line or a curve  is excited.
▪ Raster Scan : all the pixels on a screen need to be excited regardless 
the type of objects that it needs to draw.

Raster Scan Display System
▪Used in almost all the display devices.
▪Raster displays store the display primitives (line, characters, shades and 
pattern areas) in a refresh buffer.
▪Refresh buffer (also called frame buffer) stores the drawing primitives in terms 
of points and pixels components.
▪Brightness of each pixel can be controlled by control grid.
▪Each point is an addressable point in screen and memory.
▪Line cannot be drawn directly from one point to another point as in vector-
scan. It is been drawn by scanning each pixel (from left to right) of a display 
screen 
▪This causes the staircase effect also known as aliasing or jiggies.
▪Display system needs to be refreshed at a rate of 60Hz (normally).

Refresh Procedure
❖To maintain a graphics on display screen, it is required to refresh entire 
screen at some rate depending on the persistence of phosphor dots.
❖ Display device with low persistence require higher refresh rate and vice 
versa.
❖In general, raster system uses 60 to 80 frames per second i.e, 60Hz as a 
refresh rate.
❖Designing a display system with a refresh rate 60 or more is difficult. 
The beam must visit all the dots on 
a display screen in 1/60 second if 
the refresh rate is 60 frames per 
second

Interlacing 
❖First, all points on the even-numbered (solid) scan lines are displayed; then 
all points along the odd-numbered lines (dashed) are displayed.
❖ Interlaced refresh procedure: Used primarily for devices having low 
persistence.
▪In this, the beam sweeps across other scanlines from top to bottom.
▪Then after the vertical retrace takes place, 
▪Finally, the beam sweeps out the remaining line.

7-line Interlaced Scanline Pattern
❖The odd field begins with line-1. The horizontal retrace is shown dashes. The 
odd field vertical retrace starts at the bottom center. The even field vertical retrace 
starts at the bottom right.

Retracing 
❖Horizontal retrace:  As the electron beam reaches the right edge of the 
screen, it is made invisible and rapidly returns to the left edge.
▪The time taken for horizontal retrace is typically 17% allotted for a scan 
line.
❖Odd field vertical retrace - returns the beam (OFF) to the top center of the 
screen.
❖Even filed vertical retrace- returns it to the upper left corner of the screen.
▪Vertical retrace after each field requires a time equivalent to 21 scan lines.

Practice Problem  
❑ Question: Consider a raster scan based display system with 525 horizontal 
scanlines.  Assume that even field starts with the top middle of the display 
screen. If the aspect ratio is 4:3, then answer the following questions: 
▪ How many scanlines are there in each of the field (Odd/Even field)?
▪ How many scan lines are visible out of  525 scanlines?
▪ Number of pixel grids in one full scanline is………
▪ Time available for the beam to access and display a pixel is ………

Practice Problem  
❑ Question: Consider a raster scan based display system with 525 horizontal 
scanlines.  Answer the following questions: 
▪ How many scanlines are there in each of the field (Odd/Even field)?
▪ How many scan lines are visible out of  525 scanlines?
❖ Solution:
▪This is because, the vertical retrace after each field requires a time  
equivalent to 21 scan lines.
▪So, for each filed we have time to display:  (525/2)-21=241.5
▪So, for both fields together, we have:
▪                     241.5x2 = 483 lines to display.
▪  This is the reason for 42 (=525-483) invisible lines.
